*** A SECOND, NEW, INDEPENDENT DEFECT FOUND WHILE CONFIRMING THE FIRST, AND FIXED. The live pitchlaw probe printed the SAME 8-value d-sweep for every one of the five target heights (0.6, 1.9, 2.6, 4.5, 8.0 m) -- bit-for-bit identical pitch at every d -- and the trace's own `lock_height_m` field read exactly 1.9 in all 40 rows regardless of which archetype was locked. Traced to source: `game/src/sim/camera.js:targetHeight()` reads `t.archetype_id`, a property `game/src/sim/entities.js:makeEntity()` never sets on a spawned entity -- a real enemy carries `id` (the archetype/species key, == `stat.id`, e.g. "cam_boss_mid") and `eid` (the per-instance handle), never `archetype_id`. `t.height_m` (the function's second fallback) is not set either. So EVERY locked enemy the game has ever spawned -- a 0.6 m rat and an 8.0 m great boss alike -- was framed by the camera as the bare `_default` of 1.9 m. RI-CAM03 SD's entire size-dependent pitch/aim law (`size_bias(h) = 2.20 x max(0, h-2.5)`, the aim-point head/chest blend) was DEAD CODE against any entity the running game actually produces; it only ever executed inside `cam-pitch-instrument.mjs`'s synthetic sim, which sets `archetype_id` and `height_m` by hand and never goes through `spawn()`. This is the deeper, camera-side twin of the already-documented renderer defect (mesh.scale.y hardcoded to 1 except when DEAD -- the visual half of the same story): both the picture drawn and the framing that photographs it were blind to declared enemy size, for two unrelated reasons in two different files.

FIX: `targetHeight()` now tries `t.archetype_id || t.id` before falling through. Purely additive -- no entity field changes shape or value, `archetype_id` is still tried first for any caller that already sets it (the synthetic sim does). RULES.md rule 4/6 applied properly: confirmed the OLD code goes red on a REAL-entity-shaped target object (id only, no archetype_id, no height_m) via `git stash` on camera.js alone -- PRE-FIX all four heights (0.6/1.9/4.5/8.0) settle at the identical -12.858 deg with lockHeight pinned at 1.9; POST-FIX the same four inputs settle at -16.080/-12.858/+9.377/+32.000 deg with lockHeight reading 0.6/1.9/4.5/8 exactly, matching the values the synthetic-sim tests already trusted. The two arms differ, and the pre-fix arm reproduces the live browser probe's own symptom (identical rows across h) exactly -- three independent readings (browser probe, hand-shaped bare-Node pre-fix, hand-shaped bare-Node post-fix) agree with each other and with the mechanism.

*** LIVE BROWSER CONFIRMATION LANDED (reports/w1-06/... not written to the canonical probe path this round, raw JSON in this round's transcript): `node tools/camera/cam-probe.mjs --probe pitchlaw` against the FIXED camera.js, run through the real spawn() path (no hand-shaped objects). `lock_height_m` now reads exactly 0.6 / 1.9 / 2.6 / 4.5 / 8 for the five dummy archetypes -- it read 1.9 for all five before the fix, in the identical probe, same session. Pitch now genuinely diverges by height: h=0.6 settles -19.5..-8.6 deg across d, h=2.6 settles -9.9..-4.3, h=4.5 settles +8.1..+13.8 (rises then eases as the arm outpaces the size term), h=8.0 pins at the +32 deg locked-band ceiling at EVERY distance 2-14 m (the great boss's size term simply exceeds the band; the arm correctly shortens to ~2.45-2.47 m there via the pitch-arm scale table, and --gain elsewhere already showed this is a genuine clamp, not the old runaway -- G~0 at this h,d). The only failing check left in this probe is `monotone_in_distance`, the same pre-existing d2->d3 dip of ~0.1-0.3 deg present before this round's fixes too (a minor base-pitch clamp-kink, not touched this round, not related to either defect fixed here).

R2's ORIGINAL FINDING (the -50 pin), NOW CONFIRMED LANDED IN game/src/sim/camera.js AT HEAD before this round started: the up vector in basis() was built as up = right x fwd, which at yaw=0/pitch=0 is (0,-1,0) -- pointing at the ground -- and up.y = -cos(pitch) for the WHOLE legal pitch band. project()'s NDC y was therefore sign-inverted, and containSteer's `(tY>0?1:-1)*rate` correction drove the pitch AWAY from the target: a positive-feedback loop that ran to the -50 deg locked floor and pinned the view down for the rest of any fight, PAST the kill. The current source (game/src/sim/camera.js:552-643, function lockOrientation) now measures the pitch target's elevation over the PIVOT (pitch-independent baseline) instead of the camera's own pitch-dependent position, which was the actual closed loop.
